blocks.prompt: 5. Discuss domain, range, and graph of the function \(f(x) = 3^{x}\).
blocks.explanation:
\(3^{x}\) is an exponential function \(a^{x}\) with base \(a = 3 > 1\).
We must give its domain and range and describe and sketch its graph.
Plan: go through the properties of section 1.4.2 (domain, positivity, range, intercepts, increasing, one-to-one, asymptote), then plot a table of values, as in Example 7.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 3^{x}\), base \(a = 3\).
To find: domain, range and the graph.
Method: \(a^{x}\) with \(a > 1\): use the properties of exponential functions from 1.4.2 and plot points from a table.

Domain
\[\text{Dom } f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\, = \mathbb{R}\]
Why: \(3^{x}\) has a value for every real \(x\) (positive, negative, zero or irrational).

Positivity, continuity and range
\[3^{x} > 0 \text{ for all } x\]
\[x \to \infty:\ 3^{x} \to \infty\]
\[x \to -\infty:\ 3^{x} = \dfrac{1}{3^{-x}} \to 0\]
\[\text{Range } f = \,]0, \infty[\]
Why: a positive base raised to any power is positive. \(f\) is continuous, so it takes every value between its two limits 0 and \(\infty\), but never 0 itself.

Intercepts
\[f(0) = 3^{0} = 1\]
\(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\); no \(x\)-intercept.
Why: put \(x = 0\) for the \(y\)-intercept; \(3^{x} = 0\) has no solution because \(3^{x} > 0\).

Strictly increasing (and so one-to-one)
If \(x_{1} < x_{2}\), then
\[3^{x_{2}} = 3^{x_{1}} \cdot 3^{x_{2} - x_{1}} > 3^{x_{1}}\]
Why: \(x_{2} - x_{1} > 0\) and the base \(3 > 1\), so \(3^{x_{2}-x_{1}} > 1\). The graph rises from left to right, and every horizontal line meets it at most once.

Horizontal asymptote
As \(x \to -\infty\), \(3^{x} \to 0\), so \(y = 0\) (the \(x\)-axis) is the horizontal asymptote.
Why: the curve gets as close to the \(x\)-axis as we like on the left but never touches it.

Table of values and graph
\(x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2\) give \(f(x) = \frac{1}{9}, \frac{1}{3}, 1, 3, 9\).
Plot the points and join them with a smooth rising curve (figure).
Why: each step of 1 to the right multiplies the height by 3.
Check: the answer key gives Dom \(f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\), Range \(f = \,]0, \infty[\) and the same rising graph through \((0, 1)\).
blocks.final_answer: Dom \(f = \,]-\infty, \infty[\), Range \(f = \,]0, \infty[\). The graph passes through \((0, 1)\), has no \(x\)-intercept, lies above the \(x\)-axis, is strictly increasing (one-to-one) and has the horizontal asymptote \(y = 0\) as \(x \to -\infty\).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of f(x) = 3 to the power x for x from minus 6 to 2. The curve lies above the x-axis, approaches the x-axis on the left (asymptote y = 0), passes through (minus 2, 1/9), (minus 1, 1/3), (0, 1), (1, 3) and (2, 9), and rises steeply to the right.
answer_figure.caption: Graph of f(x) = 3^x: through (0, 1), increasing, asymptote y = 0
